mainTopic: The forty-eight covenants on every מצוה, the blessings and curses at הר גריזים and הר עיבל, and the start of the משנה on ברכת כהנים
overview: This amud starts by finishing a ברייתא that counts the covenants (בריתות) made on every מצוה. There are sixteen at each place the Torah was given, and three places, so forty-eight in all. רבי שמעון swaps הר גריזים and הר עיבל for the אהל מועד. The גמרא ties this to the מחלוקת between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא about whether the details of the Torah were given at סיני. רבי שמעון בן יהודה multiplies the covenants by 603,550, one for every Jew. רבי adds a further layer, which רב משרשיא explains as being a guarantor for a guarantor. Next, רבי יהודה בן נחמני teaches that the whole passage of curses is about adulterers, and proves it from the curse on making an idol. A ברייתא then learns from one פסוק that the blessing comes before the curse, that blessings and curses take turns, and that the blessings are said exactly like the curses. Finally, a new משנה begins to explain how ברכת כהנים is said in the מדינה and in the מקדש.

steps.title: Counting up to sixteen covenants
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its count: four aspects, doubled to eight, doubled again to sixteen covenants for each מצוה at one place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Four. Four and four make eight. Eight and eight make sixteen.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is finishing a count of how many covenants were made on each מצוה at one gathering, and arrives at sixteen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each מצוה has four aspects: learning, teaching, guarding and doing. These come once as a general statement and once in detail, which makes eight. Eight blessings plus eight curses make sixteen.

keyTerms.meaning: "that makes" (used when adding up a total)
covenant
general statement and detailed statement

phrases.english: Four. Four and four make eight.
phrases.notes: The first "four" closes the list just before this line: learning, teaching, guarding and doing.

phrases.english: Eight and eight make sixteen.
phrases.notes: One set of eight is blessings and the other is curses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the count that the ברייתא began earlier on the daf (at הר גריזים and הר עיבל).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At one gathering, sixteen covenants were made on each מצוה.

steps.title: The same sixteen at Sinai and at the plains of Moab
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the same sixteen covenants were also made at סיני and at ערבות מואב, and brings פסוקים as proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same was true at סיני and at ערבות מואב, as it says: "These are the words of the covenant that ה׳ commanded משה..." And it is written: "Guard the words of this covenant..."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא shows from פסוקים that covenants were also made at two more places: סיני and ערבות מואב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק speaks of a covenant in the land of מואב, alongside the one made at חורב (which is סיני). This tells us that a full set of sixteen covenants was made at each of these places too.

keyTerms.meaning: the plains of מואב, where משה taught the people before he died
as it says (introduces a פסוק)
and it is written (brings a second פסוק)
etc.: the rest of the פסוק

phrases.english: And so too at Sinai,
and so too at the plains of Moab,
as it says: "These are the words of the covenant

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה ה׳ אֶת מֹשֶׁה וְגוֹ׳,
phrases.english: that ה׳ commanded Moshe, etc."
phrases.notes: דברים 28:69. The rest of the פסוק mentions both the land of מואב and חורב, which is סיני.

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב: ״וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם אֶת דִּבְרֵי הַבְּרִית הַזֹּאת וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: And it is written: "Guard the words of this covenant, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן בְּסִינַי, וְכֵן בְּעַרְבוֹת מוֹאָב, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the count of sixteen to two more places.
steps.raayaObject: That covenants were made at סיני and at ערבות מואב as well.

steps.title: Forty-eight covenants on every מצוה
steps.stepSummary: Three places with sixteen covenants each give forty-eight covenants on every מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes out that there are forty-eight covenants on each and every מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds up the total: sixteen covenants at each of three places makes forty-eight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three places are הר גריזים and הר עיבל (counted together as one), סיני, and ערבות מואב. Sixteen times three is forty-eight.

keyTerms.meaning: it comes out / the result is
forty-eight

steps.whatToRemember: 16 covenants per place × 3 places = 48 covenants on every מצוה.

phrases.english: It comes out: forty-eight covenants
phrases.notes: Sixteen at each of three places: הר גריזים and הר עיבל, סיני, and ערבות מואב.

phrases.english: on each and every מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds up the totals from the earlier steps.

steps.title: רבי שמעון swaps the mountains for the Tent of Meeting
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון does not count הר גריזים and הר עיבל. Instead he counts the אהל מועד in the desert.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון takes out הר גריזים and הר עיבל, and puts in the אהל מועד in the desert.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives a different list of the three places where the covenants were made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He still ends up with three places. But he leaves out the ceremony at the two mountains and counts the אהל מועד instead. The total of forty-eight stays the same; only the list of places changes.

keyTerms.meaning: takes out / excludes
puts in / includes
the Tent of Meeting, where ה׳ spoke to משה in the desert
the two mountains where the blessings and curses were said after entering ארץ ישראל

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון is not arguing about the number forty-eight. He is only arguing about which three places count.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon takes out
Mount Gerizim and Mount Eival,
and puts in the Tent of Meeting in the desert.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מוֹצִיא הַר גְּרִיזִים וְהַר עֵיבָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different list of places from the one in the first opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three places are סיני, the אהל מועד, and ערבות מואב, not הר גריזים and הר עיבל.

steps.title: The argument depends on רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the two opinions follow a known מחלוקת. רבי ישמעאל holds that only general rules were given at סיני and the details came at the אהל מועד. רבי עקיבא holds that everything was given at סיני, repeated at the אהל מועד, and said a third time at ערבות מואב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They follow the argument of these תנאים, as a ברייתא teaches. רבי ישמעאל says: the general rules were said at סיני, and the details at the אהל מועד. רבי עקיבא says: general rules and details were said at סיני, repeated at the אהל מועד, and said a third time at ערבות מואב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now speaks in its own voice. It explains that רבי שמעון's different list comes from an older מחלוקת between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי עקיבא, the full Torah was given at the אהל מועד too, so it counts as a full place for covenants. That is רבי שמעון's view, and רבי שמעון was רבי עקיבא's student. According to רבי ישמעאל, the אהל מועד only completed what סיני began, so the first opinion counts the mountains instead.

keyTerms.meaning: a dispute
תנאים: the sages of the משנה period
general rules
details
and they were said a third time

steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא shows that a small difference in counting covenants comes from a big question: was the whole Torah, with all its details, given at סיני?

phrases.english: And they follow the dispute of these Tannaim,
as it was taught: Rabbi Yishmael says:
General rules were said at Sinai
and the details at the Tent of Meeting.
Rabbi Akiva says:
General rules and details were said at Sinai,
and repeated at the Tent of Meeting,
and said a third time at the plains of Moab.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רבי שמעון's different list by tying it to an earlier מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון follows רבי עקיבא: the full Torah was given at סיני, at the אהל מועד, and at ערבות מואב.

steps.title: No מצוה lacks forty-eight covenants
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by saying that every מצוה written in the Torah had forty-eight covenants made on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no מצוה written in the Torah that did not have forty-eight covenants made on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא closes with its main point: every single מצוה has forty-eight covenants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree on this total. They only argue about which three places count, so the number forty-eight holds either way.

keyTerms.meaning: and there is no (literally, "and you do not have")
were made (a covenant is "cut")

steps.whatToRemember: Whichever list you follow, every מצוה in the Torah has forty-eight covenants.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין לָךְ כׇּל דְּבַר מִצְוָה וּמִצְוָה
phrases.english: And there is no מצוה at all
that is written in the Torah
on which there were not made
forty-eight covenants.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לָךְ כׇּל דְּבַר מִצְוָה וּמִצְוָה שֶׁכְּתוּבָה בַּתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא's closing line and confirms the total.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Every מצוה in the Torah had forty-eight covenants made on it.

steps.title: Each covenant was made once for every Jew
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יהודה says in the name of רבי שמעון that the forty-eight covenants on every מצוה were made 603,550 times.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן יהודה from כפר עכו said in the name of רבי שמעון: Every מצוה written in the Torah had forty-eight covenants made on it, and each covenant was made 603,550 times.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement takes the count of forty-eight covenants and multiplies it by the number of Jews in the desert.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 603,550 is the number of men counted in the desert. The usual explanation is that each Jew took on the covenant for himself and also as a guarantor for every other Jew. So each covenant was made once for every person.

keyTerms.meaning: Covenants, binding agreements
Were made (literally, 'were cut'), the word used for making a covenant
A man from the village of עכו

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אִישׁ כְּפַר עַכּוֹ
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda, a man of the village of Akko
said in the name of Rabbi Shimon:
There is no single מצוה
that is written in the Torah
on which there were not made
forty-eight covenants
of six hundred thousand
and three thousand five hundred and fifty.
phrases.notes: That is 603,550, the number of Jewish men counted in the desert.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the total of forty-eight covenants from step 6 and multiplies it by the number of Jews.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each of the forty-eight covenants on every מצוה was made 603,550 times, once for each Jew.

steps.title: רבי says each individual Jew had 603,550 covenants
steps.stepSummary: רבי repeats רבי שמעון בן יהודה's statement and adds that, as a result, each single Jew carries 603,550 covenants.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: According to רבי שמעון בן יהודה, every מצוה had forty-eight covenants made 603,550 times. It comes out that every single Jew has 603,550 covenants.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי quotes the earlier statement and then draws a further conclusion from it about every individual Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי starts from the same number and takes it one level further. He applies the 603,550 to each person, which multiplies the count again. The גמרא will ask in the next step what exactly he is adding.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes out, it follows
According to the words of

phrases.english: Rabbi said:

phrases.aramaic: לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אִישׁ כְּפַר עַכּוֹ
phrases.english: According to the words of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda of the village of Akko
who said in the name of Rabbi Shimon,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לְךָ כׇּל מִצְוָה וּמִצְוָה שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה
phrases.english: there is no single מצוה in the Torah
on which there were not made
forty-eight covenants
of six hundred thousand
and three thousand five hundred and fifty.
It comes out that for each and every Jew
there are six hundred thousand
and three thousand five hundred and fifty.
phrases.notes: The word 'covenants' is left out but understood: each person has this many.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי: לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אִישׁ כְּפַר עַכּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats step 7 and draws a further conclusion from it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each individual Jew carries 603,550 covenants on every one of the forty-eight.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two statements?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי adds beyond what רבי שמעון בן יהודה already said.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the next step: how is רבי's statement different from the one before it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two statements sound almost the same, since both use the number 603,550. The גמרא wants to know what new idea רבי is adding.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how step 8 differs from step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical or conceptual difference exists between רבי שמעון בן יהודה's count and רבי's count.

steps.title: The difference is being a guarantor for a guarantor
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא answers that רבי also counts each Jew as a guarantor for every other Jew's role as a guarantor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said: The difference between them is a guarantor, and a guarantor for a guarantor.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא answers the question by naming the extra layer that רבי adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי שמעון בן יהודה, each Jew is a guarantor (ערב) for every other Jew. רבי adds that each Jew is also a guarantor for every other Jew's job as a guarantor. That extra layer is why the count is multiplied by 603,550 a second time.

keyTerms.meaning: A guarantor, someone responsible for another person
A guarantor for a guarantor
There is between them, this is the difference

steps.whatToRemember: Every Jew is responsible for every other Jew, and according to רבי he is even responsible for the others' responsibility.

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiyya said:
A guarantor, and a guarantor for a guarantor,
is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא: עָרְבָא וְעָרְבָא דְעָרְבָא אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי adds a second layer: each Jew is a guarantor not only for others but also for their guarantee.

steps.title: The whole passage of curses speaks about adulterers
steps.stepSummary: A new teaching begins: רבי יהודה בן נחמני says the entire passage was said only about a man and a woman who commit adultery.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן נחמני, the speaker for ריש לקיש, taught: The whole passage was said only about a man and a woman who commit adultery.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new teaching about the passage of blessings and curses. Steps 12-13 prove the claim from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, the גמרא was counting covenants. Now רבי יהודה בן נחמני makes a new claim about what the passage is really about. He says it is focused on adultery, which connects to the topic of the whole מסכת. His explanation will follow.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught publicly, explained a פסוק
The speaker who repeated a rabbi's lecture out loud to the crowd
A man and a woman who commit adultery

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Naḥmani taught,
the speaker for Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish:
The entire passage, all of it,
phrases.notes: That's the passage of blessings and curses said at הר גריזים and הר עיבל, in דברים 27.

phrases.english: was said only about an adulterer and an adulteress,

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן נַחְמָנִי מְתוּרְגְּמָנֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the covenant count and begins a new teaching about the same passage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The whole passage of blessings and curses is focused on a man and woman who commit adultery.

steps.title: Is a curse really enough for an idol worshipper?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the curse on someone who makes an idol and asks whether a mere curse is a big enough punishment for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Cursed is the man who makes a carved or cast idol.' Is a curse really all he deserves?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins proving רבי יהודה בן נחמני's claim from Step 11. It points to a curse that seems too weak for the sin it names. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עבודה זרה is one of the worst sins in the Torah. If this curse were simply about an idol worshipper, a curse alone would be far too small a response. So the plain reading must be wrong, and the פסוק must be about something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Cursed
A carved idol and a cast (molten) idol
Is it enough for him?

phrases.english: "Cursed is the man who makes
a carved or molten idol, etc."
Is a "cursed" enough for him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the proof for רבי יהודה בן נחמני's statement in Step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can a mere curse be the right response to idol worship?

steps.title: The curse is on parents whose forbidden union led their son to idols
steps.stepSummary: The curse is really about a man who had a child from a forbidden relationship. That son later left and worshipped idols, so his parents are cursed for causing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is about someone who was with a forbidden relative and had a son. The son went off among the nations and worshipped idols. His father and mother are cursed because they caused this to happen to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The curse is not on the idol worshipper himself; it is on the parents whose sin led him there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits רבי יהודה בן נחמני's claim that the whole passage of curses is about forbidden relationships. Even the curse that seems to be about idols really goes back to עריות. A curse fits the parents, who only caused the idol worship and did not do it themselves.

keyTerms.meaning: One who has relations with a forbidden relative
The nations of the world (non-Jews)
They caused it to him

phrases.english: Rather: this is one who had relations with a forbidden relative
and fathered a son,
and he (the son) went off among the nations of the world
and worshipped idols.
Cursed are this one's father and mother
for causing him this.

steps.whatToRemember: Even the 'idol' curse is read as being about forbidden relationships. That backs up רבי יהודה בן נחמני.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12 and completes the proof of Step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The curse is on the parents of a ממזר who turned to idols, not on the idol worshipper himself.

steps.title: Why does the Torah repeat which mountain gets the blessing?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks why the Torah needs the פסוק about putting the blessing on הר גריזים and the curse on הר עיבל, since other פסוקים already say this.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'Put the blessing on הר גריזים and the curse on הר עיבל.' Why does the Torah need to say this? If it's to teach which mountain gets the blessing and which gets the curse, other פסוקים already tell us that.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא begins. It points out that this פסוק seems to repeat what other פסוקים already say. That sets up the search for a new lesson in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דברים 27:12-13 already says who stands on הר גריזים to bless and who stands on הר עיבל to curse. So דברים 11:29 must be teaching something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Mount Gerizim, the mountain of blessing
Mount Ebal, the mountain of curse
Why does the פסוק need to say this?

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"And you shall give the blessing on Mount Gerizim
and the curse, etc."
Why does the verse say this?

phrases.aramaic: אִם לְלַמֵּד שֶׁתְּהֵא בְּרָכָה עַל הַר גְּרִזִים
phrases.english: If it is to teach that the blessing is on Mount Gerizim
and the curse on Mount Ebal,
it has already been stated:

phrases.aramaic: ״אֵלֶּה יַעַמְדוּ לְבָרֵךְ אֶת הָעָם עַל הַר גְּרִזִים״,
phrases.english: "These shall stand to bless the people on Mount Gerizim,"

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב ״וְאֵלֶּה יַעַמְדוּ עַל הַקְּלָלָה בְּהַר עֵיבָל״!
phrases.english: and it is written: "And these shall stand for the curse on Mount Ebal"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא about the ceremony at the two mountains.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new lesson does דברים 11:29 teach, since the mountains are already given elsewhere?

steps.title: The blessing must come before the curse
steps.stepSummary: The extra פסוק teaches the order: the blessing is said first, and then the curse.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it teaches that the blessing comes before the curse.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question. The פסוק is not about which mountain; it is about the order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names the blessing first and the curse second. Since the location is already known, that order itself becomes the lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: To put first, to say before

phrases.english: Rather, it is to put the blessing before the curse.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק teaches that the blessing is said before the curse.

steps.title: One blessing, then one curse, alternating
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא makes clear that not all the blessings come first. Instead, each blessing comes right before its matching curse.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think all the blessings are said first, and only then all the curses. So the פסוק says 'blessing' and 'curse' in the singular: one blessing comes before one curse, not all the blessings before all the curses.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible misunderstanding of the last step and corrects it using the exact wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Blessing comes first' could mean the whole set of blessings goes first. The singular words 'blessing' and 'curse' show the pattern instead: blessing, curse, blessing, curse, one pair at a time.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought
Therefore the פסוק says
Comes before

steps.confusionAlert: Don't picture a block of blessings followed by a block of curses. They take turns: one blessing, then one curse.

phrases.english: One might think that all the blessings
come before the curses;
therefore the verse says: "blessing" and "curse"
one blessing comes before a curse,
and not all the blessings come before the curses.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל יִהְיוּ כׇּל הַבְּרָכוֹת קוֹדְמוֹת לַקְּלָלוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the rule of Step 15 by showing exactly how 'blessing first' works.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blessings and curses alternate, with each blessing said just before its curse.

steps.title: The blessings are said exactly like the curses
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק links blessing and curse, so the blessings copy the curses in five ways: said by the לויים, loudly, in לשון הקודש, as a general statement plus details, and both groups answer אמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק also links blessing to curse, to teach you this. Just as the curse is said by the לויים, so is the blessing. Just as the curse is said loudly, so is the blessing. Just as the curse is said in לשון הקודש, so is the blessing. Just as the curse is said in general and then in detail, so is the blessing. And just as both groups answer אמן to the curse, so both groups answer אמן to the blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא learns one more lesson from the פסוק: it compares blessing and curse (a היקש), so the blessings follow every rule the Torah gives for the curses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah describes in detail how the curses are said, but says much less about the blessings. Because the פסוק puts the two side by side, every detail of the curses carries over to the blessings.

keyTerms.meaning: To compare two things so one learns from the other (היקש)
Levites
A loud voice
The holy language, Hebrew
A general statement and specific details
These and those, meaning both groups

steps.whatToRemember: One פסוק, three lessons: the blessing comes first; blessings and curses alternate one by one; and the blessings are said exactly like the curses.

phrases.english: And it is to compare blessing to curse,
to tell you:
just as the curse is said by the Levites,
so too the blessing is said by the Levites.
And just as the curse is said in a loud voice,
so too the blessing is said in a loud voice.
And just as the curse is said in the holy language,
so too the blessing is said in the holy language.
And just as the curse is said in general and in detail,
so too the blessing is said in general and in detail.
And just as with the curse, these and those (both groups)
phrases.notes: 'These and those' means the people on both mountains.

phrases.english: respond and say "Amen,"
so too with the blessing, these and those
respond and say "Amen."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another lesson from the same פסוק of Step 14, alongside the order rules of Steps 15-16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The blessings are said by the לויים, loudly, in לשון הקודש, as a general statement plus details, and both groups answer אמן, just like the curses.

steps.title: New משנה: How ברכת כהנים is said in the מדינה and in the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה asks how ברכת כהנים is done. In the מדינה the כהן says it as three separate ברכות, but in the מקדש it is said as one ברכה. In the מקדש the כהן also says the שם of ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: How is ברכת כהנים done? Outside the מקדש, the כהן says it as three blessings. In the מקדש, he says it as one blessing. In the מקדש, he says ה׳'s Name...
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens a new topic, ברכת כהנים. It explains two differences between saying it outside the מקדש and inside the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three פסוקים of ברכת כהנים are the same everywhere, but they are divided differently. In the מדינה, each פסוק stands alone as its own ברכה. In the מקדש, all three are said together as one ברכה. The משנה then starts a second difference: in the מקדש the כהן says the שם of ה׳. The line continues in the next part of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; the label that marks the start of a new משנה
The Priestly Blessing that the כהנים give to the people
Here: anywhere outside the בית המקדש
The בית המקדש, the Temple
ה׳'s actual Name, said as it is written

steps.confusionAlert: Here מדינה does not mean a country or state. It means any place outside the בית המקדש.
steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה is the starting point for how ברכת כהנים is said today in shuls, which follows the rules of the מדינה.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
How is the Priestly Blessing done?
In the country, he says it
phrases.notes: "The country" here means anywhere outside the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: as three blessings,
and in the Temple, as one blessing.
In the Temple, he says the Name

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic after the discussion of the ברכות and קללות at הר גריזים and הר עיבל ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the מדינה, ברכת כהנים is said as three separate ברכות. In the מקדש it is said as one ברכה, and the כהן says the שם of ה׳.
